rows.definition: internal/safecommit/checkerpin.go GuardCheckerPin: the close-arm consult a witness/grade arm calls right before accepting a run - it refuses (ReasonCheckerTampered) when the run's declared checkers drifted from their pinned baseline, and passes an un-drifted run through untouched.
rows.distinction: A PROVENANCE consult over checker BYTES (did the checkers move since pinning?) - NOT a runtime adjudication gate (it gates a graded run's provenance, not a tool call or its result) and NOT the guard kernel itself.

rows.definition: The authoring-time policy-extraction subsystem (`fak guard compile`, internal/guardcompile plus cmd/fak/guard_compile.go): turns a transcript excerpt into a draft policy via an OpenAI-compatible extractor - the build step that PRODUCES a policy manifest before any guard enforces it.
rows.distinction: An AUTHORING-TIME extractor (transcript -> draft policy), not a runtime gate that admits or refuses a call - it runs once at policy-build time and never in the live decision chain, unlike guard_mcp/guard_codex which wire an already-compiled policy into a live child.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_wire_retry.go guardMaybeRetryTransientWireCrash: the runtime decision that, when a transient wire error was observed and the retry budget allows, appends the agent's continue flag to relaunch the crashed child process.
rows.distinction: A RESTART decision (append a continue flag and relaunch the child), not a tool-call adjudication gate - it fires on a child process crash, not on a syscall or its result. Its evidence source is guardWireErrorGauge, which it reads; this function DECIDES, that one MEASURES.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_wire_retry.go guardWireErrorGauge: the recency gauge that records the last transient wire-error timestamp and exposes Consume/Recent within a 15s window (guardWireRetryWindow) - the evidence guardMaybeRetryTransientWireCrash reads to decide whether a retry is in-budget.
rows.distinction: A MEASUREMENT gauge (did a wire error happen recently within the window?), not the retry DECISION that consumes it - distinct from guardMaybeRetryTransientWireCrash which reads this gauge and decides. Gauger vs decider; the gauge never relaunches anything.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_stops.go guardStopRecord: one durable JSONL ledger row recording a single Stop-hook invocation - its typed disposition, the gauges that drove it, and transcript-derived context; versioned by the guardStopRecordSchema string ('fak.guard-stop.v1').
rows.distinction: A LEDGER ROW (the durable artifact a stop wrote), not the Stop hook gate itself (guardStopHook) that DECIDED the stop - the record is the evidence, the hook is the decision. The schema constant versions the row shape so a reader can evolve.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_slack.go guardSessionThreadSource: the 'guard-session' source-tag constant prefixing every Slack outbox row a guard session emits - progress/banner/context/status/outcome each append ':<sub>' to it to name which sub-stream the row belongs to.
rows.distinction: A source-TAG constant (names WHICH Slack thread/sub-stream a row belongs to), not the drain that SENDS those rows - distinct from startGuardSessionThreadDrain which pumps the outbox to that thread. One labels, the other ships.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_slack.go startGuardSessionThreadDrain: the goroutine starter that, on guard launch, opens the Slack outbox and drains queued rows to the resolved sessions thread (10s timeout) so a session's buffered messages ship instead of lingering.
rows.distinction: The SEND action (pump the outbox to the thread on launch), not the source-TAG (guardSessionThreadSource) that names the thread - one ships rows, the other labels them. Both concern the guard-session Slack thread but play opposite roles.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_machine_registry_windows.go machineGuardRegistryDir: the machine-level guard-control registry directory under %ProgramData%/fak/guard-control/registry (Windows), returned only when the dir exists - where the installed guard service's machine-wide state lives.
rows.distinction: A filesystem PATH (the installed guard's machine registry directory), not a gate or a decision - it LOCATES state, it does not adjudicate. Windows-only; the non-Windows stub returns empty, so it is a location resolver, never a guard component.

rows.definition: cmd/fak/guard_precompact.go normalizeGuardPreCompactMode: the validator that canonicalizes a --precompact-hook mode string to one of off/shadow/enforce, erroring on any other value - the parse step every precompact-mode flag and witnessed-done path passes through.
rows.distinction: The VALIDATOR function (string -> canonical mode or error), not the mode VALUE itself (guardPreCompactMode and its off/shadow/enforce constants) - it parses and rejects invalid input; the mode constants are the parsed result it returns, never the parser.
